analysis: The only change in this PR is one documentation row added to docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 414). It documents a new environment variable, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED. The variable selects the Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 models. The default is a probe that keeps the four-row kernel only where it matches the stock gated_delta_step bit for bit. Forced values (packed, rows) skip that check and are described as A/B measurement only. The row says the variable is read once per process and is not forwarded to LaunchAgents. I reviewed it against TB-007 (inference engine), T-007 (manipulated outputs), T-012 and T-041. It touches no key, attestation, coordinator or prefix-cache storage control. It adds no network or storage surface and no coordinator authorization input. It is a process-local, operator-controlled env var, and the operator already holds full local control (ADV-001 per TB-003). Its effect is on numerical kernel choice, not on confidentiality or attestation. The only residual question is whether a forced kernel could change output correctness, which is already covered by the existing T-007 and T-056 position that correct computation is not attested. The implementation (GatedDelta.swift) is not in the supplied evidence, so the claimed fallback, probe and not-forwarded behaviour is unverified. The excerpt is also truncated mid-row, but the visible patch shows only this one added row. The unit text contains no embedded instructions. No threat-model update is needed beyond noting that the setting exists. I found no concrete security regression.
